In the game, players aim to achieve specific combinations of cards, known as "winning hands," through actions such as drawing, discarding, pung, and kong. Mahjong not only tests memory and strategy but also integrates probability and chance, embodying profound cultural significance and social attributes. However, as Mahjong becomes a widely popular social activity, its impact on personal life has gradually become apparent. In this paper, I delve into the analysis of the effects of playing Mahjong on marital relationships, particularly the three negative effects it brings to women: Time Displacement: The uncertainty of Mahjong playing time leads to a reduction in shared time between spouses. Women may feel neglected due to the lack of companionship, leading to "Mahjong Panic Syndrome." Emotional Conflict: Mahjong playing can result in losses, and men may harbor "resentment from defeat" at the Mahjong table, which could be brought into the household and spark marital disputes. Social Isolation: Women may feel excluded from their partner's social circle if they do not participate in Mahjong activities, experiencing "marginalization at the card table." This study not only reveals the potential negative impact of late-night Mahjong returns on marital relationships but also provides new insights into communication and empathy between spouses from the perspectives of decision trees, time series analysis, and game theory. It also finds the optimal solution through Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Continuously Tunable Mid-Infrared Metalens Integrating Moiré and Pancharatnam-Berry Phases
items.summary: A varifocal mid-infrared metalens designed for focusing applications is proposed to integrate both Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) and Moiré pattern-based mechanisms for rotational wavefront control. The metalens employs two identical nanostructured discs featuring germanium (Ge) meta-atoms on calcium fluoride (CaF2) substrates, operating as birefringent half-wave retarders with 99.95% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) and 83.65% total transmission power at 2 μm wavelength. Full-wave numerical simulations demonstrate continuous focal length tunability from 45 μm to 12 μm by rotating the second disk from 30 deg. to 120 deg., corresponding to the numerical aperture values ranging from 22.99% to 68.67%. The proposed metalens maintains reconfigurable focusing regardless of the incident light polarization, while concurrently enabling polarization-controlled operation via a phase-modulation mechanism that yields inverse responses under Right Circular Polarization (RCP) and Left Circular Polarization (LCP) illuminations.

items.title: Discovering Hidden Predictive States in Kinetic Transport
items.summary: How do autonomous macroscopic transport laws emerge from kinetic dynamics, and which hidden degrees of freedom must survive coarse-graining? We address these questions by formulating kinetic state reduction as a problem of predictive sufficiency rather than conventional moment truncation. Starting from Boltzmann transport dynamics, we establish a quantitative connection between unresolved microscopic information, irreducible prediction error, and finite-horizon observability. Microscopic preparations with identical macroscopic observables but distinct subsequent evolution provide direct witnesses of incomplete dynamical closure. We develop an entropy-constrained learned state-reduction framework, demonstrated here through linear projections, that identifies the additional predictive states without prescribing their physical identities and determines their necessity through independent response tests, state deletion, and dynamical consistency. An exactly solvable three-velocity model demonstrates that a hidden higher-order moment can influence future energy transport despite identical initial energy and heat flux. Numerical experiments recover this missing direction and reveal how the required state dimension depends on observation scale, prediction horizon, preparation ensemble, and accuracy. In a synthetic 32-channel Boltzmann system, the learned representation identifies predictive combinations spanning multiple kinetic branches and relaxation groups that are not captured by low-order global moments. We further distinguish observable prediction accuracy from autonomous state closure and quantify the information retained through unresolved memory. These results establish an operational framework for testing the emergence of effective transport laws and identifying the microscopic information required for their predictive validity.

items.title: Edge turbulence controlled by topologically self-optimized fluxes in fusion devices
items.summary: The magnetic field topology undergoes a drastic transition near the separatrix in magnetic confinement fusion devices, inducing topological chaos. This phenomenon is investigated across tokamaks, stellarators, and the RFX-mod reversed-field pinch. Within this boundary region, self-optimized fluxes of shear-generated magnetic and cross-helicity, together with the ensemble-averaged magnetic moment, are hypothesized to govern plasma stability, self-organization, and transport. By treating the averaged magnetic moment as an active scalar and using the Fokker-Planck equation to reconcile kinetic and fluid descriptions, this study couples its dynamics with a novel multichannel, self-optimized helicity cascade loop. The derived spectral laws for the floating potential and ion saturation current agree with measurements from numerous experiments. Distributed chaos theory quantifies the randomness of the observed states, revealing that a narrow layer at the separatrix suppresses strong core randomness, transforming it into distributed chaos in the scrape-off layer. A constrained variational principle for active control has also been considered. Tuning Lagrangian multipliers via helicity injection drives the system toward an attractor state that stabilizes the separatrix shear layer, suppresses edge-localized modes, and spreads the heat load, using magnetic reconnection as a nonlinear solver. This framework circumvents conventional diffusive limitations, providing an analytical foundation to model heat-load patterns and stochastic ripple loss in next-step devices.

items.title: Electrohydraulic Fields Generated by Active Transport at Tissue Interfaces
items.summary: Living cells and tissues can generate complex patterns of electric fields and fluid flows which can play important role in physiology. Both, fields and flows are rooted in ion transport across biological interfaces: cell membranes and epithelial cell layers. Here we develop a unified electrohydraulic framework that combines electric fields, osmotic pressures, and fluid flows, emphasising their couplings. We consider an active, permeable interface that drives electrohydraulic fields in the surrounding bulk. We show that spatially heterogeneous ion transport acts as a distributed current source, generating long-range electric fields, osmotic gradients, and fluid flows. Using this framework, we show that patterns of ion pumping at cell and tissue boundaries can simultaneously produce large-scale electric fields and fluid flows due to electrohydraulic coupling. A key insight is that an external electric field and an internal dipolar pumping pattern can be physically equivalent and can generate the same pattern of ion current and fluid flows. The induced dipolar osmotic pressure can drive self-propulsion through bulk osmotic coupling, with a mobility determined by interfacial permeability and system size, a mechanism distinct from classical electrophoresis or electro-osmosis. We further show that for strong fields a new effect emerges. Nonlinear coupling can lead to isotropic swelling of a hollow ball of cells. This can explain recent experiments on epithelial organoids. Finally, we show that feedback between ion transport and resulting electric fields can drive spontaneous symmetry breaking, generating dipolar or multipolar fields and patterns. Our work highlights the importance of electrohydraulic coupling in the emergence in currents and fields in the biological systems.

items.title: Spin-wave circulation in unbounded ferromagnetic film
items.summary: A key challenge in spin-wave computing is steering spin waves through circuits without wave distortion or reflections. This often results in 1D propagation scenarios, which hinder applicability in 2D magnonic circuits. We demonstrate experimentally a novel approach using a hard magnetic spherical microparticle to guide spin-waves onto a closed path in a plain thin YIG film. The particle stray field induces a radially symmetrical magnetization landscape, which allows spin-waves to loop around. In parallel, we conducted micromagnetic simulations reproducing the experimental conditions, which confirm the circulation of spin-waves over several loops around the particle. This work demonstrates the possibility to steer spin-waves onto a circular path using inhomogeneous magnetic landscape, as well as advancing scalable spin-wave-based information processing technologies.

items.title: Real-Time 24-hour Ahead Forecasting of Solar Energetic Particle Events with SEPNET-PRISM-R
items.summary: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, operationally defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the >10 MeV channel, threaten spacecraft systems, astronaut safety, and high latitude aviation, yet continuous real-time forecasting with adequate lead time remains difficult. We present SEPNET-PRISM-R, a near-real-time system that issues hourly, 24 hour ahead probabilistic SEP forecasts. The model integrates multimodal solar data - including active region patches, flare features, coronal mass ejection (CME) characteristics, and historical proton flux - to concurrently predict SEP occurrences, peak proton flux, soft X-ray flux, and CME velocity, with the primary objective being SEP forecasting. Building on existing literature, SEPNET-PRISM-R enhances operational performance by incorporating a postprocessing module that enables cross-validated decision making and interpretable quantification of feature importance. The training dataset spans from February 1986 to September 2025, with subsequent forecasts generated sequentially through the present via a real-time space weather prediction platform that provides predictive probabilities, feature attributions, and historical analogs, enabling more reliable and informed operational decision-making. The proposed framework substantially suppresses false alarm rates while maintaining robust event detection capabilities, as evidenced by case studies and aggregate statistics.

items.title: Physics-informed sampler for solver-free data generation in operator learning
items.summary: Neural operators offer fast surrogates for parametric PDEs but typically rely on costly datasets generated by repeated numerical solves. We propose a physics-informed sampler (PI-sampler) that generates PDE-consistent input--solution pairs without numerical PDE solves. The sampler draws candidate solution fields from neural-network priors and uses automatic differentiation to evaluate the governing differential, boundary, and initial-condition operators, yielding consistent training tuples by construction. Unlike solution-first methods based on analytical bases or precomputed solutions, it requires neither problem-specific basis functions nor seed simulations. The resulting PDE inputs follow an implicit pushforward distribution, which can be characterized for linear operators in the Gaussian-process limit of Bayesian neural networks but is generally non-Gaussian for nonlinear operators. We integrate the PI-sampler with a function encoder and Transformer-based neural operator and test it on reaction--diffusion equations, Poisson equations on parameterized geometries, time-dependent Sine--Gordon dynamics, a five-dimensional PDE, and flexible-cylinder vortex-induced vibration. The models generalize to independently prescribed forcing distributions, zero forcing, mixed boundary conditions, and unseen geometries. Experiments with DeepONet confirm that the generated data also support other operator architectures. In problem-specific benchmarks, sampling is approximately 51 times faster on CPU and 850 times faster on GPU than numerical solvers. The PI-sampler thus provides an efficient approach to data generation and augmentation that complements high-fidelity simulation.

items.title: Diffractive neural networks for mode-sorting with flexible detection regions
items.summary: Mode-sorting is a procedure that decomposes a light field into a basis of transverse modes, directing each mode into a separate spatial location, allowing the constituent mode intensities to be measured simultaneously. We demonstrate a mode-sorter based on a diffractive optical neural network and show that it is advantageous to include the output detection regions into the trainable set of parameters of that network. This approach outperforms traditional mode-sorting methods, achieving lower crosstalk levels for the same efficiency. For example, in sorting 25 Hermite-Gaussian modes with a 3 plate sorter, at 12 % efficiency, the experimentally measured crosstalk decreases from 37.5 % for fixed detection to 8.7 % for flexible detection.

items.title: Connecting the Hydrodynamics of Polymeric Fluids and Active Nematics
items.summary: We establish a correspondence between the continuum descriptions of polymer solutions and active nematics, two seemingly disparate but well-studied complex fluids. Through a mapping of the governing equations, we demonstrate that polymeric fluids can be interpreted as deformable, contractile, high-temperature active nematics, with an effective activity controlled by polymer extension. Using numerical simulations under Kolmogorov flow, we construct a phase diagram connecting the nematic and polymer limits, highlighting how their one- and two-dimensional instabilities depend on deformability. This encompasses both a flow-suppressed regime, in which active stresses oppose the imposed flow, and a transverse instability that generates secondary flows and leads towards elastic turbulence. The transverse instability is facilitated by spatial gradients in activity, which arise naturally in extensible polymers through variations in chain extension. We further show that the transition into the well-known traveling arrowhead structures in elastic turbulence is marked by the emergence of charge $\pm 1/2$ topological defects in the polymer director field, indicating emergent nematic ordering of stretched polymers. Our results establish a unified framework connecting polymer and active matter hydrodynamics, with implications for low-Reynolds-number turbulence, active polymer systems, and the mechanics of deformable living matter.

items.title: Momentum Distribution of a mass-imbalanced three-body system across the Efimov-Unatomic transition
items.summary: We investigate the single-particle momentum distribution, the two-body contact and three-body tail coefficients of mass-imbalanced three-body systems at the critical dimension $D_c$, where the transition between discrete and continuous scale invariance takes place as the spatial dimension is tuned between three and two dimensions. We show that the asymptotic momentum distribution at $D_c$ is governed by a distinct logarithmic scaling structure, which differs fundamentally from both the log-periodic behavior of Efimov states and the power-law scaling of the unatomic regime. This structure contains an additional quadratic-logarithmic contribution, characterized by the asymptotic coefficient $C_3''$, which leads to a finite and well-defined description of the momentum tail at the transition. The coefficient $C_3''$ depends sensitively on the mass imbalance, changing sign across different mass configurations and vanishing for identical particles. For heavy-light-light configurations, the subleading three-body term vanishes at a characteristic momentum, leaving the leading two-body contribution at the order retained in the asymptotic expansion. The physical accessibility of this cancellation depends on the separation between the trimer size and the interaction range. We further analyze the narrow intermediate region connecting the Efimov and unatomic regimes, here identified as an intermediate scaling regime, whose extent and properties are strongly controlled by the mass ratio. These results establish the critical dimension as a regime with emergent scaling properties and provide quantitative momentum-space signatures for probing the transition between discrete and continuous scale invariance in few-body quantum systems.

items.title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
items.summary: The flow of molecularly confined water has attracted considerable interest in recent years. Yet despite their exquisite character, current nanofluidic devices cannot probe molecular water flow beyond the linear-response regime, while nanomechanical force- based approaches have produced markedly inconsistent results. Here, using tuning- fork-based atomic force microscopy, we tackle these limitations by measuring the full linear-to-nonlinear, shear-dependent viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at various two-dimensional material interfaces -- demonstrating pronounced rate effects in water flow response. The observed rheological behaviors are remarkably analogous to that of macroscopic soft glassy yielding materials and fully captured by a non-linear model accounting for the shear-induced acceleration of the dynamics -- a hallmark of disordered supercooled and metastable systems. We further unveil a pronounced pressure-induced slowdown in nanoconfined water dynamics, with relaxation times extending into the microsecond range and marked material dependence. These results reveal non-linear, glassy rheology as a general feature of interfacial water and offer a route to tunable, non-linear nanofluidic elements.

items.title: Physics-constrained graph closures and working-point conditioning for a fast surrogate of linac beam dynamics
items.summary: When a graph neural network estimates a physical quantity, its frame, edge direction, aggregation and feature normalization decide which laws it can break. Wrong choices leave systematic errors the loss never registers. We build a linac beam-dynamics surrogate on this observation. Space charge, short-range wakefields and coherent synchrotron radiation enter as bounded closures on analytic kernels, on graphs whose frame and direction follow the interaction and whose symmetry makes the net space-charge self-force vanish for any weights. Verified without training, with randomized weights, the invariants break by five to eight orders of magnitude once the responsible feature is inverted. Per-working-point models constrained by the rms envelope equation are distilled into one model conditioned on 15 machine settings. On the 18.4~m L0+L1 section of the Shanghai soft x-ray free-electron laser linac, this model predicts the transverse beam envelope at 50 unseen settings to about $7\%$, with the centroid trajectory and emittance, in 0.38~s on a single Quadro RTX 6000 GPU. Training is instead dominated by a normalization choice, a data-derived output range for the beam size: at all 16 working points it lowers the starting error 2.2- to 8.5-fold and fixes the convergence speed. The remaining accuracy differences between hybrid and data-driven architectures vary with the working point and with the density of observation. The held-out error scales roughly as $N^{-0.6}$ with the corpus size $N$. Whether the physics pays off where collective effects are strong, as in a magnetic bunch compressor, is in the next phase of our study.

items.title: Cooperative control of dissipative qubits: steering along the fastest dissipative contraction
items.summary: In the control of dissipative quantum systems, the slow relaxation modes usually set the ultimate manipulation timescale. We show that this bottleneck can be bypassed when dissipation itself is used as the engine of the transfer. For a qubit with non-unital, anisotropic Bloch relaxation characterized by the ratio $κ=T_1/T_2>1$, coherent control can only rotate the Bloch vector, whereas the bath alone can change its length. The fastest transfer between two thermal states therefore consists in steering the Bloch vector, at every instant, along the direction in which the bath contracts it most rapidly. This direction is obtained in closed form and lies slightly beyond the equatorial plane. With strong pulses, the resulting minimum transfer time is a fraction of $T_2$, instead of several $T_1$ for passive relaxation. With bounded fields, the Pontryagin maximum principle yields a bang--singular--bang synthesis whose singular arc is precisely this fastest-contraction direction, and the minimum time exceeds its strong-pulse limit by a correction inversely proportional to the field amplitude. We also determine the full time--energy Pareto front: moderate accelerations require little energy, and the time optimum lies at its steep, high-energy end. Off-axis targets are treated within the same framework; their only additional benefit is a shorter final rotation. These results apply directly to magnetic-resonance spins, nitrogen-vacancy centers and superconducting qubits, all of which operate deep in the strong-pulse regime.

items.title: Wavepackets in subsonic elliptical jets: coherent-structure eduction and linear modelling
items.summary: We study coherent structures extracted from time-resolved particle image velocimetry (TR-PIV) measurements of isothermal elliptical jets with aspect ratio of 1:2, at Mach numbers 0.4 and 0.7. The velocity snapshots are decomposed according to the D$_2$ symmetry. Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition (SPOD) is then used to identify coherent structures. Modelling is performed using three-dimensional parabolised stability equations (3D-PSE) based on linearisation about the time-averaged mean flows. A comparison between SPOD and 3D-PSE results shows alignment of SPOD and single-mode PSE structures of up to 70\%. A linear combination of PSE solutions, obtained from the family of initially unstable local modes, leads to SPOD-PSE alignment of up to 90\%. Limitations are observed at low frequencies and near the nozzle and are attributed to the existence of non-modal amplification mechanisms. The study shows that coherent structures in turbulent elliptical jets can be educed using the D$_2$-SPOD approach, and modelled using 3D PSE.

items.title: Disentangling forced and internal components in observed climate evolution using spatiotemporal deep learning
items.summary: Attribution of observed historical climate evolution to externally forced change and internal variability is fundamental to understanding climate change and evaluating climate models. Yet such attribution remains challenging because the forced response is intertwined with internal variability in observations. Here, we develop a convolutional long short-term memory network (ConvLSTM) to disentangle these two components. Trained and evaluated using large-ensemble simulations from multiple climate models, ConvLSTM consistently outperforms existing model-based, statistical, and machine-learning approaches. Applying ConvLSTM to observations reveals an evolving spatial pattern of the forced response and substantial contributions from internal variability to recent multidecadal climate trends. For several key climate features whose attribution remains debated, ConvLSTM indicates that internal variability amplified the forced reversal of Atlantic interhemispheric temperature asymmetry, dominated the observed La Niña-like warming pattern over the equatorial Pacific and the associated precipitation decline over southwestern North America since 1980, and modulated Arctic amplification around its nearly constant threefold forced value. Comparison between the ConvLSTM-estimated and model-simulated forced responses reveals broadly consistent patterns but also important discrepancies, with climate models simulating stronger Northern Hemisphere warming, weaker subtropical high intensification, and smaller land precipitation declines. Overall, ConvLSTM provides a robust framework for attributing historical climate evolution and evaluating the fidelity of climate models

items.title: Measuring electron density and electromagnetic fields in low-density laser-driven plasmas using proton radiography
items.summary: In this paper, we describe a novel technique for inferring electron density in laser plasmas from proton-radiography data. Proton radiography is primarily a diagnostic for imaging electromagnetic field structures in such plasmas. In the presence of strong field gradients, `caustic' features arise and are broadened by the process of collisional scattering between the imaging protons and the plasma. This effect has a well defined density dependence, allowing for a robust measurement of electron number density. We validate the method on data from the turbulent-dynamo experiments performed at the Omega laser facility (with electron densities in the range of ${\sim}10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$), achieving good agreement with values obtained from Thomson scattering, x-ray imaging and simulations. This research enables one of the most robust techniques for measuring electromagnetic fields on laser-plasma experiments to simultaneously provide density measurements along the same line of sight, improving our ability to diagnose such plasmas.

items.title: A Multimodal Engineering GraphRAG Framework for Post-Wind-Event Building Assessment and Recovery Inference
items.summary: Post-event building assessment requires linking observed physical damage to its consequences for safety, habitability, functionality, and recovery. Yet post-disaster evidence is often heterogeneous, incomplete, and distributed across images and reconnaissance reports, while recovery models typically require structured engineering inputs. This study develops a multimodal engineering Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) framework that connects post-wind-event damage evidence to physical consequences, building-condition states, recovery actions, and downtime. Image- and text-based evidence is transformed into a provenance-preserving, component-level representation distinguishing confirmed damage, explicit negative evidence, unresolved conditions, and temporary measures. Graph-aligned retrieval combines comparable building scenarios with explicit engineering relationships, while compatibility, contradiction, evidence-precedence, and abstention mechanisms constrain inference under partial observability. Recovery actions are derived from supported damage-consequence relationships, and downtime uncertainty is propagated through an action-dependency network using Monte Carlo simulation. The framework is demonstrated for tornado-affected low-rise residential buildings using reconnaissance and image-based evidence. Comparisons with BaselineRAG and Structured Baseline RAG show improved agreement for key building-condition and recovery outcomes, together with traceable engineering reasoning and preserved evidence provenance. Ablation analyses demonstrate the contributions of engineering context, evidence safeguards, and graph-path traversal. The results support transparent, recovery-oriented assessment from incomplete multimodal post-event evidence.

items.title: Variable-Resolution Scattering Reveals Ensemble Properties
items.summary: SAXS/SANS determine the size and structure of particles and macromolecules in solution. However, the conventional low-angle determination of the radius of gyration, Rg, cannot separately resolve its scattering-weighted mean and the width of its distribution. Because the apparent Rg includes a contribution from ensemble variance, the distribution width is required even to recover the mean Rg. Here, we introduce TENOR-SAXS, a method for estimating the scattering-weighted width of an Rg distribution by applying two anisotropic digital smearings to a single 2D scattering image. Comparing the smeared images provides curvature information unavailable from the conventional radial profile. The resulting observables require no explicit model of the native instrumental point-spread function and show only weak sensitivity over the range of native resolutions typical of SAXS measurements examined here. Analytical expressions are derived in the low-angle and narrow-distribution limits for ensembles described by a known or independently constrained single-particle form factor. For verification, we simulated scattering by particles with several form factors and ensembles with different size distributions, all agree well with the analytical theory. To leading order, the principal observable depends on the scattering-weighted mean and variance rather than on the distribution's functional form or higher moments. For simulated data corresponding to feasible synchrotron exposure times for biological samples, the distribution width and, expressed as a fraction of its mean, was recovered with a typical discrepancy of ~0.1, while the scattering-weighted mean Rg was recovered with ~2% relative discrepancy. TENOR-SAXS thus provides a framework for estimating ensemble width from existing 2D scattering data without explicit instrumental desmearing and for correcting the variance contribution to the apparent radius

items.title: Response-state Learning for Transferable Vibrational Spectroscopic Characterization with Electron Prior
items.summary: Vibrational spectral prediction can become inaccurate when localized stereoelectronic environments perturb intermediate response states and high-risk response units dominate characteristic spectral fingerprints, making prediction across external chemical space difficult. SO(3) Equivariant Neural Kalman Networks (SENK) form a response-state cascade that combines an equivariant transformer backbone for Hessian, dipole-derivative and polarizability-derivative learning, an Equivariant Neural Kalman bridge for state-dependent refinement and reliability sensing, and an NBO-informed electronic-prior pathway coupling consistency regularization with bounded, branch-specific guided spectral calibration. SENK outperforms DetaNet on QM9S and QMe14S while preserving full-spectrum IR and Raman fidelity from small molecules to drug-like systems. SENK remains stable and selectively improves spectrally sensitive features in biomolecular systems with complex stereoelectronic effects. It therefore integrates tensor prediction, reliability diagnosis and physics-informed calibration, supporting transferable vibrational spectroscopy from molecular systems to functional molecular materials.

items.title: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
items.summary: We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox. Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied. We identify the assumptions underlying this modelling and highlight two key features, fast scrambling dynamics and entanglement as a resource, that underpin the information release in the model. We argue that this reasoning exemplifies a broader change in how information is used in black hole physics, in which quantum information theory now provides a useful operational modelling framework. This application avoids earlier philosophical objections insofar as it is not based on epistemic ignorance and does not regard information as a substance. This line of reasoning has become central to the debate and, as such, warrants greater attention from the philosophy of physics community.

items.title: Learning global river system hydrodynamics with a topology-informed foundation model
items.summary: Accurate river prediction is essential for water, food, and energy security, yet extending it reliably from sparse in-situ gauges to the full river network remains an open challenge. Although machine learning has transformed Earth-system modelling, the same sparse and uneven observations have largely confined its advances for rivers to discrete basins rather than connected river systems. Here we introduce GraphRiverCast (GRC), a topology-informed river foundation model for reach-level prediction across the global river network. Exploiting the connectivity and energetics of rivers, it is trained on sparse gauges and predicts daily multivariate hydrodynamics with no prior river conditions. GRC outperforms strong physics-based and machine-learning models. Attribution experiments show that, compared with standard autoregressive models that rely more on temporal recurrence, GRC reconstructs river states from topology and forcing, learning the dynamics themselves and inheriting the self-correcting character of river systems. Its skill therefore barely decays with lead time, even far beyond its training horizon. It also generalises to ungauged reaches and finer-resolution networks, bringing reliable hydrodynamic prediction to poorly monitored regions. More broadly, harnessing the structure and energetics of a system offers a strategy for machine learning in other observation-limited Earth systems.

items.title: Mechanical quality factor estimation from a nonlinear optical cavity response
items.summary: Intrinsic damping rate and quality factor ($Q$) are key parameters in optomechanical systems. However, in high-Q devices, their measurement is often challenging because probe-induced dynamical backaction (DBA) and the need to resolve and accurately track the mechanical resonance limit the performance of state-of-the-art techniques. Here, we introduce an all-optical ringdown method in the unresolved-sideband regime that exploits the nonlinear, time-averaged optical response induced by strong mechanical motion. We derive an analytical model of the time-averaged optical cavity response probed by a weak frequency-scanning laser. During the evolution of the mechanical oscillator, the excited motion modulates the Lorentzian lineshape into a double-horned profile whose peak separation enables an accurate estimation of the modulation amplitude. Tracking this response during the mechanical ringdown allows the intrinsic damping rate to be determined without resolving the mechanical oscillation. We apply the method to a density-modulated phononic crystal membrane placed inside a high-finesse cavity and obtain mechanical quality factors consistent with independent measurements on the same platform. Our method requires a minimal optical setup, while offering an in situ diagnostic and reduced impact from probe-induced DBA and robustness against measurement noise. Finally, the model can describe other resonant systems dispersively coupled to coherent frequency modulations, providing new insights and measurement strategies that expand beyond the optomechanical platform.

items.title: Pulse Shape Model for a Light Enhanced Phonon Detector
items.summary: COSINUS has tested prototype NaI-based cryogenic scintillating calorimeters with a composite design, in which the transition edge sensor (TES) is fabricated on a separate carrier crystal coupled to the NaI target. Measurements with the composite detectors showed deviations from the known pulse shape description for cryogenic calorimeters and did not reveal an identifiable nuclear recoil population during a neutron calibration. In this work we present a new pulse shape model which provides an explanation to these observations and that laid the foundation for the development of the final COSINUS phonon detector design named remote TES (remoTES). We demonstrate that the first COSINUS detector prototypes featured a phonon channel with signal enhancement by light absorption in the carrier, namely a light enhanced phonon detector. This design offers for the first time the chance to use a single channel phonon detector for particle discrimination. We present recent results using a novel pulse shape fitting method based on the Bayesian inference software package BAT.jl.

items.title: Enhancement of Li and Na Storage in Janus HfSSe Monolayers by Co-Induced Electron-Deficient Chalcogen Sites: A First-Principles Study
items.summary: The growing demand for high-capacity, fast-charging, and durable rechargeable batteries has intensified the search for advanced electrode materials, with two-dimensional materials offering large surface-to-mass ratios and short ion-diffusion pathways. Here, pristine and Co-doped Janus HfSSe monolayers were investigated as anode materials for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries using first-principles density functional theory. Pristine HfSSe was found to be dynamically stable and exhibited a 0.85 eV band gap, while Co substitution shifted the Fermi level toward the valence-band region. Adsorption of the first Li or Na layer induced metallic behavior, thereby improving charge transport. Co doping strengthened alkali-metal binding, with the most favorable Li and Na adsorption energies changing from -2.6125 and -1.9800 eV to -3.7405 and -3.0529 eV, respectively. Co doping created electron-deficient sites that enhanced Li/Na binding. Co-doped HfSSe accommodated up to four Li layers and three Na layers, increasing the theoretical capacities from 555.43 to 776.19 mAh/g for Li and from 370.29 to 582.14 mAh/g for Na. The average open-circuit voltages were 0.62 V for Li and 0.29-0.30 V for Na, with minimum migration barriers of 0.2153 and 0.1044 eV, respectively. These results identified Co-doped Janus HfSSe as a promising anode material for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries.

items.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
items.summary: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($β> 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$). Across the catalog, we find an average occurrence rate of $\approx 2.6$ events per Carrington rotation, a median event duration of $\approx 9.0$\,hours, and a median physical thickness of $\approx 7.4 \times 10^6$\,km. Furthermore, approximately $\approx 15\%$ of detected SBCs interact with interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on average, with this proportion rising up to $33\%$ during solar maximum. These CME-associated events exhibit systematically longer durations (median of $10.0$\,hours), $54\%$ larger physical thicknesses, and higher average solar wind velocities. Notably, all high-velocity SBC events ($> 600\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$) are exclusively driven by CME interactions, demonstrating local plasma pile-up and structural entanglement resulting from fast CMEs overtaking the ambient slow background. The \textsc{SBCross} catalog serves as an updated successor to the classic SBC list by L. Svalgaard, delivering a standardized, open-access resource for the heliophysics community to systematically investigate sector boundary transitions.

items.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo for Efficient Estimation of Drag-Coefficient Statistics in Rarefied Satellite Aerodynamics
items.summary: Very-low-Earth-orbit analyses require reliable uncertainty estimates for the aerodynamic drag coefficient, but repeated direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) evaluations are expensive. We investigate whether cheaper collisionless models can reduce the computational cost of estimating DSMC-based drag statistics across different geometries. We also test whether improvements in the mean carry over to a variance reconstructed from two separately estimated raw moments. In the multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) estimator, PICLas DSMC provides the high-fidelity response, while PICLAS test-particle Monte Carlo (TPMC) and the free-molecular Sentman panel model provide low-fidelity control variates. The benchmark contains four canonical Cube cases and scaled GOCE-like and CHAMP-like surface models. Each paired evaluation uses the same physical-input sample in all three models, and the reference values use 450 physically distinct DSMC evaluations per case. At the same estimation cost, DSMC-TPMC-Sentman MFMC reduces the RMSE of the mean drag coefficient in every tested case and budget, with median gains of 1.50-3.03. Variance estimation is less consistent: the three-model estimator improves three cases, performs close to HF-only Monte Carlo in two cases, and fails for GOCE-like. In that case, Sentman is only weakly correlated with the DSMC variance-related responses. Removing Sentman eliminates the negative estimates and improves the variance RMSE, although the decision to remove it was made after inspecting the results. MFMC therefore improves mean estimation reliably at reduced computational cost, but each low-fidelity model must be assessed separately for variance estimation.

items.title: Deriving Interplanetary Sector Boundary Crossings using Potential Field Source Surface Modeling
items.summary: The Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) and associated interplanetary sector boundaries fundamentally structure the solar wind environment, modulating coronal mass ejection (CME) evolution and solar energetic particle transport. In this study, we evaluate the capability of a static Potential Field Source Surface (PFSS; $R_{ss}=2.5R_\odot$) coronal model to directly map interplanetary sector boundary crossings from the Sun to 1 au without dynamic heliospheric propagation models. We compare ballistically transported HCS crossings derived from GONG-ADAPT and SDO/HMI magnetic maps against sector boundary crossing observations from the SBCross catalog. PFSS modeling reproduces the large-scale interplanetary magnetic field topology well ($J\approx0.50$), achieving hit rates (POD) of 0.64 for GONG-ADAPT and 0.76 for HMI. Carrington synoptic maps outperform flux-transport modeled maps, suggesting that the short-term observational noise from data assimilation degrades topological matching more than map "aging". Predictive skill shows a strong solar cycle dependence, performing significantly better during solar maxima (POD=0.70-0.81) than solar minima (POD=0.56-0.67), attributed to more distinct crossings due to higher HCS inclination angles during maximum. Matched events exhibit travel times close to ballistic estimates of 4.8-4.9 days with an average timing difference centered near zero ($\pm1.1$ days) and 90% of events within $\pm 1.8$ days. The hit rate of HCS structures that interact with CMEs does not degrade (POD = 0.67-0.83), despite propagating $\approx7$ hours faster on average, implying that the CME interaction causes only minor structural changes to the HCS. Larger timing differences (>24 hours) are associated with flatter current sheets. Overall, static PFSS extrapolations offer a computationally inexpensive, effective approach for mapping global sector boundary structure.

items.title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
items.summary: The spatial evolution of a turbulent boundary layer at $Re_τ= 652$ developing across a finite spanwise oscillating wall is investigated with normalised oscillation period of $T^+ \approx 101$ and amplitude $A^+ \approx 7$, yielding a drag reduction of 32\%. The spatial distribution of skin friction is estimated adopting a recently introduced near-wall data nonlinear regression method based on the arctangent function, which circumvents the requirement of high wall-normal resolution to capture the viscous sublayer. The method viability is assessed against reference DNS data, and the trends of measurement errors from experimental data are well reproduced. The local impact of the control action is examined by evaluating the spatial development of scalar fields of turbulence statistics as well as conditional quadrant analysis to link the onset and recovery transients to turbulence events. The boundary layer response is observed to follow an exponential decay law for the skin friction spatial evolution. The decay length-scale corresponds to $0.6$ boundary layer thicknesses $δ$ for the onset transient and $0.9δ$ for the recovery one. The same exponential fit applied to the Reynolds stresses yields a response within $0.5δ$, with the exception of the shear stress peak, that requires a significantly longer distance.

items.title: Diffusion MRI protocol design for reliable parameter recovery: a unified framework across biophysical models
items.summary: Reliable microstructural parameter estimation in diffusion MRI (dMRI) critically depends on the acquisition protocol. Yet, common protocol design criteria may not fully reflect estimator bias, parameter constraints, and nonlinear fitting behavior in complex inverse problems. Here, we introduce Protocol Optimization via Loss Assessing Parameter Recovery (POLAR), an end-to-end framework that searches the continuous acquisition space and directly minimizes multiparameter recovery error through noisy signal simulation and the chosen model fitting. We demonstrate POLAR spanning distinct microstructural environments: the Cylinder-Zeppelin model for white matter, Neurite Exchange Imaging (NEXI) for gray matter, and Cellular Exchange Imaging (CEXI) for permeable cells. Across independent held-out parameter sets, POLAR consistently outperformed model-specific reference designs, reducing RMSE by up to $50\%$ for Cylinder-Zeppelin and $74\%$ for CEXI, while reducing NEXI exchange time bias by $70\%$. These gains across distinct biophysical models, acquisition settings, and reference design strategies demonstrate the benefit of optimizing acquisition protocols through the downstream parameter-estimation problem. POLAR provides a flexible, model-specific and estimator-aware framework for designing dMRI protocols tailored to the microstructural parameters and experimental conditions of interest.

items.title: Quantum Limits of Blind Superresolution Imaging
items.summary: Quantum estimation has shown that spatial-mode measurements can avoid Rayleigh's curse, but the fundamental precision limits are usually formulated for a known point-spread function (PSF). We show that, for two equally bright incoherent sources sharing an unknown static, shift-invariant complex-amplitude response, the local quantum information for separation is exactly the same as in the known-PSF case. In a quantum semiparametric formulation, the equality follows from the orthogonality of the separation score to the nuisance tangent space generated by all admissible PSF perturbations. We propose two receivers to access this information: momentum-resolved Hong--Ou--Mandel interference (MR-HOM), which acquires half the small-separation quantum information per signal photon without reconstructing the PSF, and a tomography-assisted symmetric logarithmic derivative receiver (TA-SLD), which asymptotically attains the full bound under explicit recovery conditions. These results provide a route toward blind superresolution without prior PSF calibration in microscopy, astronomy, and other optical imaging systems with uncertain responses.

items.title: Operator learning for efficient quantum computation
items.summary: An efficient implementation of quantum algorithms is often hindered by the lack of efficient primitives for operators and state preparation. This limits both the ability of near-term quantum hardware to simulate complex problems and the potential of fault-tolerant algorithms to achieve practical quantum advantage. To address this, we propose a framework that maps discrete operators onto compact, structured quantum circuits. The resulting variational circuits can be tailored to the connectivity and long-range interaction of the target hardware. The learning process employs backpropagation together with a cost function that efficiently optimizes unitary operators and non-unitary --dense or sparse-- operators using only a single ancilla qubit for block encoding. Additionally, we introduce a regularization term that reduces the approximation error. The approach is validated for both quantum mechanical and engineering applications. In the former case, we learn propagators that arise in native quantum problems --such as quantum simulation and quantum chemistry-- and achieve improved resource scaling in comparison to standard Suzuki--Trotter expansions. In the latter case, we demonstrate the approach's ability to implement the second-order central finite difference approximation of the Laplace operator --relevant for solving partial differential equations-- while improving upon current error metrics. The final example deals with learning a dense, non-unitary operator that arises in the analysis of inviscid potential flow around an airfoil. These results motivate the extension of the framework to a broader class of operator-synthesis problems beyond the prototypical engineering and quantum applications considered here.

items.title: Quantifying the Threat: A Bayesian Probabilistic Framework for Heavy Metal Health Risks among Children in the Densu Basin, Ghana
items.summary: Groundwater in Ghana's Densu River Basin remains a key domestic water source, but multi-metal contamination threatens children's health. Previous deterministic hazard index assessments provide limited treatment of uncertainty, co-exposure, and spatial variability. This study applies a Bayesian probabilistic framework for non-carcinogenic risk assessment using 94 groundwater samples and measurements of Fe, Mn, Ni, Pb, Cd, and As. A Bayesian regression model propagates parameter uncertainty and accounts for contaminant co-occurrence. Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo is used for posterior inference, while inverse distance weighting generates spatially continuous risk surfaces. Pb, As, and Cd dominate cumulative risk. Posterior predictive results indicate that approximately 31% of sampling sites have a probability greater than 0.5 of exceeding a hazard index (HI) of 1. The risk surface is highly heterogeneous, with a posterior mean of 0.372 and a standard deviation of 0.416. High-risk zones often reflect moderate co-exposure rather than extreme contamination by a single metal. The framework provides uncertainty-aware, spatially explicit information to support groundwater monitoring, risk mitigation, and public health planning in data-limited regions.

items.title: Interface-dominated sliding compound drops
items.summary: We investigate compound drops composed of two immiscible nonvolatile partially wetting liquids that slide down an inclined homogeneous smooth solid substrate based on a mesoscopic hydrodynamic two-layer model in full-curvature formulation. First, we briefly investigate the reference case of a liquid drop that stationarily slides on a liquid layer representing an adaptive substrate. Subsequently, we focus on sliding compound drops employing a parameter study to identify qualitative transitions between different drop configurations and time-periodic behavior as well as the underlying bifurcation structure. After analyzing the dependence of drop velocities and dynamic Young and Neumann angles on driving force, also the influence of the ratios of drop volumes and viscosities is briefly considered. An accompanying discussion of the lateral dissipation profile is used to explain the encountered dependence of drop velocity on their configuration. Finally, we consider the time-periodic fusion-overtaking-splitting behavior found outside the existence range of the stationary sliding compound drops.

items.title: Inelastic spreading of viscoelastic drops
items.summary: When a liquid drop impacts a solid surface, rebound and splashing are known to be suppressed by additives that induce elastic effects; however, the influence of elasticity on the maximum spreading radius remains debated. The difficulty lies in isolating elastic resistance from the enhanced spreading caused by viscous shear thinning. Here, we experimentally decouple these effects by investigating Boger fluid drops (constant-viscosity solutions with high elasticity) of polyethylene oxide (PEO) and polyacrylamide (PAAM). We demonstrate that elastic properties do not alter the maximum spreading ratio, even at high concentrations up to 1000 ppm. We formulate an energy balance that accounts for the inertial, capillary, viscous, and elastic contributions, and yields a dimensionless criterion ($Γ$) that estimates the degree of elastic effects. We show that $Γ\ll 1$ for all impact conditions tested, demonstrating that elastic effects are energetically negligible during droplet spreading, opposite to what Weissenberg and Deborah numbers would predict.

items.title: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
items.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. Here we show that quantum-light-driven HHG opens an additional information channel through the photon statistics of the emitted harmonics. Using the Haldane Chern insulator and the time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele topological insulator, we calculate helicity-resolved equal-time intensity correlations and identify a common enhancement of high-order harmonic correlations in the topological phases. For the Haldane model, a dichroic correlation constructed from opposite helicity channels reverses sign with the Chern number. These signatures originate from the distinct nonlinear response sampled by quantum fluctuations of the driving field and are absent from the corresponding mean harmonic spectra as a common classifier. Our results establish photon-correlation spectroscopy as a route to interrogate topological matter with quantum light and provide a bridge between strong-field solid-state physics and quantum optics.

items.title: A Topological Spin on Racetrack Memory: Stability and Transport of 360° Domain Walls in Magnetic Nanotubes
items.summary: Magnetic racetrack memory requires localized carriers that combine rapid motion, resistance to perturbations and a detectable signal. Here we show how a 360° domain wall in a hollow ferromagnetic tube combines these properties within a single continuous magnetic shell. Two successive magnetization reversals form a bound object whose surrounding domains point in the same direction. Analytical energetics and micromagnetic simulations establish its finite separation, recovery from tested perturbations and current driven transport without microscopic Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction or a maintaining field. The texture's winding resists unwinding while radial rotation carries an energy cost, providing a specific control over stability. Relative rotation of the constituent spins accounts quantitatively for additional displacement during current onset. The wall supports motion at hundreds of metres per second, with transient velocities approaching one kilometre per second at stronger drive. A prepared seven-bit pattern retains its carriers and local readout contrast after pulsed transport and recovery. Curved-track and differential-current tests identify radial stiffness and drive uniformity as controls for intact motion. These results establish a physical basis for fast, locally distinguishable tubular magnetic bits and identify a continuous switching pathway that can be targeted by tailored excitation.

items.title: Towards a Complete Kerr Soft-Hair Theory: Integrability, Counterterm Equivalence,and Quantum State Counting
items.summary: The horizon symmetry construction of Haco, Hawking, Perry, and Strominger yield two Virasoro central charges 12J after a specified Wald-Zoupas correction. Turning that calculation into a black hole microstate theory requires separate control of nonlinear charge integrability, the allowed counter-term class, and quantum state multiplicities. We formulate exact local and global integrability tests, prove uniqueness of the counter-term coefficients within a one-parameter ansatz, and identify the quotient in which a physically meaningful uniqueness theorem must be stated. A coadjoint-orbit model supplies globally defined classical moment maps, while unitary highest-weight modules supply an explicit algebraic quantum realization for macroscopic positive angular momentum, neither construction is proved equivalent to the gravitational phase space. A character calculation shows why a single Virasoro representation, despite having the desired central charge, does not provide the required large-central-charge entropy. We derive a curvature improvement invisible to the constant mode, quantize a regulated area-boost corner polarization, and find a continuous kinematic spectrum with divergent Gibbs trace. Explicit local modular CFT spectra with identical central charges yield different finite-temperature entropies, demonstrating that the available symmetry and quantum consistency data do not select the microscopic theory. We give a conditional sufficiency theorem and a concrete sequence of calculations needed to establish a gravitational completion.

items.title: Rapid Variability of Radiative Signatures from Driven Relativistic Reconnection
items.summary: Rapid variability in energetic flares is a distinctive feature of high-energy emission from many magnetically dominated astrophysical sources. We investigate the radiative variability of driven relativistic magnetic reconnection using Particle-in-Cell simulations of strongly magnetized flux tubes pushed to merge at driving speed $v_{\rm push}$. This setup captures the onset of reconnection and provides a controlled model for single reconnection-driven flares near compact objects, where magnetic structures can be twisted, sheared, and forced to merge by turbulent accretion flows or relativistic frame dragging. We find that the merger efficiently accelerates particles into nonthermal distributions, producing synchrotron emission whose variability tracks the reconnection phases. We identify two regimes: a quasi-steady, weakly driven regime for $v_{push}\leq0.1\,c$, and strongly driven regime for $v_{\rm push}>0.1\,c$. The transition occurs when the driving exceeds the typical inflow-to-outflow velocity ratio of $\sim0.1$ in steady collisionless relativistic reconnection, i.e., the average rate at which reconnection can process incoming flux, potentially providing an additional source of variability. The lightcurves rise on $1$--$3$ light-crossing times of the reconnecting region, and the particle spectra develop power laws with index $p\simeq1.8$--$2.4$. These timescales are compatible with observed variability in high-energy sources, including the very-high-energy flares of M87$^*$ and the $γ$-ray flares of the Crab Nebula, making this model a viable framework for rapid flaring in active galactic nuclei and pulsar wind nebulae.

items.title: Enhanced orbital-angular-momentum dimensionality and spatial-spectral decoupling in thin-film SPDC
items.summary: Thin-film spontaneous parametric down-conversion, due to the relaxed phase-matching condition, generates photon pairs that are extremely broadband in frequency and angle and highly entangled in time/frequency and position/momentum. Here we show that it also provides a very broad orbital angular momentum (OAM) spectrum, which, in contrast to the case of bulk crystals, is decoupled from the frequency spectrum. To demonstrate it experimentally, we generate photon pairs in a $7~μ\mathrm{m}$-thick lithium niobate film and compare them with those from a $500~μ\mathrm{m}$-thick periodically poled lithium niobate crystal under identical pump conditions. The thin-film source exhibits a substantially broader OAM spectrum, with the azimuthal Schmidt number almost 9 times larger than that of the bulk source. On this highly entangled state, we perform quantum-state tomography in selected two- and four-dimensional OAM subspaces, demonstrating high-purity maximally entangled states. These results highlight thin nonlinear films as a promising platform for high-dimensional quantum-state generation with weak spatial--spectral coupling.

items.title: ACE2-NEMO: Coupling an ML atmospheric emulator to a full-depth dynamical ocean model
items.summary: Understanding how fast atmospheric variability shapes slow climate variability and sensitivity remains a central challenge in Earth-system science. Recent advances in machine-learned (ML) atmospheric models have demonstrated remarkable skill on weather timescales, but their emergent behaviour in a fully coupled climate system remains largely unexplored. We present early results from a new hybrid modelling framework, in which the ACE2 ML atmospheric emulator is interactively coupled to the NEMO ocean model. We report on a set of 70-year coupled simulations (1950-2020 historical forcing and fixed-1950s control). These experiments represent, to our knowledge, one of the first multi-decadal integrations of a machine-learned atmosphere interacting with a full-depth dynamical ocean. Several historical and fixed-1950s control simulations from the fully dynamic global coupled climate model EC-Earth, which has the same ocean component used in ACE2-NEMO, are also considered for comparison. We assess the behaviour of the coupled system, with particular focus on low-frequency tropical variability and the climate response to greenhouse-gas forcing. Analysis of potentially emergent El Nino-like variability reveals realistic fast timescale air-sea coupling in the tropical Pacific, but the temporal variability is unrealistic, with very low amplitude oscillations; this appears to be due to weak atmospheric feedback in the tropical Pacific. The response to CO2 forcing shows initial agreement with EC-Earth3P but deviates due to reduced downward short-wave radiation in ACE2. These results provide a unique test of physical realism and generalisability for atmospheric emulators and evaluate the possible role of entirely machine-learned components in next-generation Earth system models.

items.title: A high-fidelity numerical database for free-stream-turbulence-induced transition under varying pressure gradients
items.summary: Free-stream-turbulence-induced transition under streamwise-varying pressure gradients, as encountered on turbine blades, has received much less attention in high-fidelity simulations than its zero-pressure-gradient counterpart. The ERCOFTAC T3 experiments provide a carefully documented reference for this problem and remain central to transition-model calibration. Complementing them with full-field, three-dimensional data opens new opportunities for the development of physics-based and machine-learning transition models. To this end, wall-resolved implicit large-eddy simulations of the T3A, T3B, and T3C2--C5 flat-plate cases are performed with a high-order compressible solver, using an upstream slip-wall block that lets the synthetic free-stream turbulence develop up to the leading edge. The simulations reproduce well the measured transition locations, integral quantities, and velocity profiles, and predict a separation bubble near the end of the plate for the lowest-Reynolds-number case T3C4. As the Reynolds number decreases and transition moves into the adverse-pressure-gradient region, the mechanism evolves continuously from classical bypass transition to transition governed by the tendency of the laminar boundary layer to separate, up to separation-induced transition. Intermittency, conditioned statistics, and Reynolds-stress budgets document this evolution and the associated non-equilibrium effects, which challenge current RANS transition models.

items.title: Floquet density response in laser-assisted fast-electron scattering from solids
items.summary: We extend the Bethe--Floquet formalism of Joachain and coworkers, originally developed for laser-assisted electron--atom collisions, to inelastic scattering of fast electrons from a many-body condensed-matter target in a time-periodic light field. At first order in the projectile--target interaction, the general Floquet--Fourier cross section separates into exact laser-dressed projectile kernels and a matrix-valued Floquet density response of the target. For spatially structured or translationally non-invariant systems, the latter is the bi-momentum Floquet structure factor; its momentum diagonal defines the Floquet generalization of the dynamic structure factor, constrained by Hermiticity, positivity, and sum rules. As a controlled realization of the general projectile kernel, an eikonal--Volkov approximation for slowly varying inhomogeneous fields yields a finite-momentum-resolution convolution of the target response. In the homogeneous-field dipole limit, the projectile kernel reduces to Bessel-function sidebands and the cross section takes the familiar Bethe--Floquet form. The Floquet density correlator separates exactly into the outer product of the pump-induced coherent mean density and connected fluctuations. In the straight-trajectory nonrecoil limit, the coherent, target-elastic sector defines the weak-coupling PINEM amplitude; repeated coherent insertions generate the PINEM Bessel ladder, with an explicit no-double-counting prescription for combining this channel with connected losses. As worked examples, we evaluate the connected, target-changing cross section analytically for a metal in the Drude and diffusive limits, recovering Bessel-weighted plasmon-loss and diffusive combs, and for a driven two-level model that exhibits off-diagonal Floquet coherences through Bessel-channel interference.

items.title: Phase shifts and fluctuations from motional, relativistic, and dark-matter effects in ion-trap clocks
items.summary: Ions possess both center-of-mass motion and internal states, rendering trapped-ion optical clocks susceptible to perturbations of both degrees of freedom, which results in systematic shifts and fluctuations with motional and relativistic origins. We develop a quantum theory that connects these effects to filter functions determined by the employed pulse sequences and show how the interrogation can be tailored to suppress or enhance specific perturbations. Our treatment includes laser frequency noise and motional effects such as recoil and Doppler shifts, micromotion and excess micromotion, as well as state-dependent trap imperfections and accelerations, e.g., caused by Stark shifts. We further account for relativistic effects including time dilation and the mass defect, and show how the same framework can be applied to hypothetical dark-matter signals. By considering ensemble-averaged phases and their variances, we characterize both systematic shifts and fluctuations, while asynchronous operation relative to the Paul-trap drive allows motional fluctuations to average down between runs. Our results provide a unified framework for characterizing and controlling the systematic and statistical contributions that determine the trueness and precision of trapped-ion optical clocks.

items.title: A Discrete Amplitude-to-Time Conversion Circuit for TDC-Based Readout of Fast Scintillation Detectors
items.summary: Fast timing measurements with scintillation detectors commonly employ leading-edge discriminators and time-to-digital converters (TDCs). Many applications also require an energy-related observable for estimating the deposited energy and correcting time-walk effects. Time-over-threshold (ToT) is frequently used for this purpose, but its relationship to pulse amplitude can be severely degraded by undershoot, ringing, and other distortions of the detector pulse tail. This work presents a discrete analog front-end circuit for amplitude-to-time conversion that is insensitive to pulse-tail distortions. An analog multiplexer and a high-speed comparator implement a sample-hold-discharge stage: upon leading-edge detection, the detector pulse amplitude is sampled near its peak and stored on a capacitor, which is subsequently discharged at a controlled rate. The resulting digital pulse width encodes the sampled amplitude, while the leading edge preserves the timing information. The circuit was designed for a short recovery time and a total dead time below 100~ns, making it suitable for high-rate detector readout. The approach enables simultaneous timing and amplitude measurements through a single TDC channel. An eight-channel front-end card implementing this concept was characterized using generated test pulses. The measured transfer function is approximately linear up to input amplitudes of 0.5~V and extends beyond 2~V, with a low-amplitude conversion gain of approximately 27~ps/mV. The estimated relative amplitude precision falls below \SI{0.5}{\percent} for input amplitudes above 0.5~V. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a low-complexity, multichannel amplitude-to-time converter for TDC-based detector readout, offering an alternative to conventional ToT measurement when pulse-tail distortions compromise amplitude estimation.

items.title: Giant Spin-to-Charge Conversion by Tailoring Magnetically Proximitized Topological Dirac Semimetal
items.summary: The role of magnetic proximity on topological surface states (TSSs) and spin-to-charge conversion efficiency is studied in Fe/topological Dirac semimetal $α$-Sn heterostructures. As $α$-Sn thickness increases (9-38 nm), the damping constant of Fe peaks at 25 nm and then decreases. Theoretical modeling links this to long-range magnetic proximity effects (MPE) that suppress TSSs at the Fe/$α$-Sn interface while opening an exchange gap at the opposite interface. At 25 nm, we achieve an inverse Edelstein length of -3.1$\pm$1.0 nm, one of the highest values at room temperature, highlighting MPE's importance in spintronics.

items.title: Effect of interfacial water structure on the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions
items.summary: Weakly hydrated anions tend to partition to macromolecular surfaces, leading to salting-in at low salt concentrations. Recent studies have linked this partitioning to disruption of the interfacial water network. Here, we investigate the role of interfacial-water-network disruption as an indirect driving force for the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions and its interplay with direct solute-anion and anion-cation interactions using computer simulations. We study the adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ and I$^{-}$ ions on a model extended solute that interacts with water and ions only via van der Waals interactions. To probe the indirect contribution, we increase the effective solute size while simultaneously decreasing the attractive solute-water and solute-ion interactions, resulting in progressively greater disorder in the interfacial water network in pure aqueous solutions. Our results show that iodide adsorption increases despite weaker direct solute-iodide interactions and correlates with greater disruption of the interfacial water network, although iodide remains depleted overall. In contrast, preferential adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ decreases, but the rate of decrease becomes smaller at higher levels of interfacial-water-network disorder. This suggests that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption partly compensates for the decrease in SCN$^{-}$ adsorption caused by weaker direct solute-SCN$^{-}$ interactions. Our results highlight that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption promotes the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions on macromolecular surfaces, while the extent of adsorption also depends on direct solute-ion interactions and anion-cation pairing. This interplay may be particularly important in mixed-salt solutions, where the presence of strongly hydrated anions can also disrupt the interfacial water network.

items.title: Clarifying tipping terminology
items.summary: The notion of tipping points and related terminology have so far had inconsistent and sometimes confusing definitions in both scientific and popular literature. While it is difficult for the scientific community to align popular usage of the term tipping point with a precise definition, technical usage of related terms would benefit from greater consistency and rigor. Toward this end, we offer a systematic set of terms to clarify formal communication around potential tipping dynamics, with focus on examples from Earth system dynamics.

items.title: infomeasure-rs: A High-Performance Rust Library for Information-Theoretic Measures and Estimators
items.summary: Information theory has become a standard tool across the natural and social sciences, yet practical use is limited by estimator choice, fragmented software, reproducibility, and computational cost. We present infomeasure-rs, an open-source Rust library that brings a broad set of information-theoretic measures and estimators into one self-contained, type-safe package. It covers entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information, transfer entropy, conditional transfer entropy, cross-entropy, and the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences, with discrete (plug-in and bias-corrected), kernel, ordinal, and nearest-neighbour estimators, including the Rényi and Tsallis families, and exposes local and global values and significance testing through a consistent trait interface. It ships as a single portable binary with no runtime dependency and is continuously validated against a reference implementation. On a single central processing unit (CPU) core, and even without its GPU or parallel paths, it is the fastest of the packages we compared across languages, matching the closest packages only for plug-in discrete entropy and substantially faster for mutual information, the conditional and transfer measures, and the kernel, ordinal, and generalised-entropy estimators. The optional GPU and multi-threaded paths accelerate selected continuous estimators further. The library is open source and, to our knowledge, the most complete information-theory package for Rust.

items.title: Constrained modularity maximization in complex networks via branch-and-price
items.summary: Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. We study constrained modularity maximization with restrictions on the number of communities, must-link and cannot-link relations, and general resource constraints. While fast heuristics can provide high-quality solutions, they generally lack optimality guarantees, whereas exact mathematical-programming approaches can become computationally demanding as the network size and constraint complexity increase. We develop a unified optimization framework offering complementary heuristic and exact solution methods. These include a constrained Louvain heuristic for feasible solution generation, a column-generation heuristic with graph-partitioning-based pricing, and exact branch-and-price algorithms using mixed-integer linear programming and sparse mixed-integer quadratic programming formulations for the pricing subproblem. We develop a cutting-plane procedure providing independent upper bounds to assess solution quality when exact optimization cannot be completed. Experiments on 11 unconstrained networks with up to 1,005 nodes and 30 constrained instances with up to 379 nodes demonstrate the complementary roles of these methods. The column-generation heuristic rapidly improves the constrained Louvain solutions across the tested constraint classes, while branch-and-price using the sparse quadratic formulation solves 29 of the 30 constrained instances to optimality within a one-hour time limit. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. Overall, the framework guides method selection to balance computational time, solution quality, and optimality guarantees.

items.title: Second-order difference-frequency effects on floating wind turbine responses: full-QTF modelling and experimental comparison
items.summary: Accurate prediction of low-frequency responses is important for the dynamic assessment of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), as second-order difference-frequency wave loads can contribute substantially to platform motions and mooring loads. Their relative importance, however, remains less well established when aerodynamic and hydrodynamic low-frequency excitations coexist under operating conditions. This study develops an efficient time-domain formulation for full difference-frequency quadratic transfer function (QTF) loading using bandwidth truncation and integrates it into a fully coupled model of the IEA 15 MW turbine on the VolturnUS-S semi-submersible platform. Numerical predictions are compared with 1:70-scale real-time hybrid wave-basin experiments covering both irregular wave-only and combined turbulent wind-wave conditions. Three hydrodynamic formulations are compared: linear wave excitation, Newman's approximation, and the full-QTF model. Under wave-only conditions, second-order difference-frequency loading substantially improves the prediction of surge and the associated mooring response, particularly in energetic sea states, with the full-QTF model generally providing the closest agreement with measured low-frequency spectra and peak-amplitude distributions. Under combined wind-wave conditions, low-frequency thrust fluctuations dominate near rated wind speed, reducing the relative importance of difference-frequency wave excitation, whereas its contribution becomes more apparent at higher wind speeds as thrust fluctuations diminish. Overall, the full-QTF model provides the most consistent improvement over the linear and Newman models, with maximum surge standard deviation discrepancy from measurement under the most energetic wave conditions less than 18%, with smaller discrepancies for heave, pitch, and mooring tensions.

items.title: A Catalog of Dispersive Ionospheric and Plasmaspheric Arcs from Cislunar and Lunar-surface GNSS Radio Occultations
items.summary: This dataset is a catalog of 263 dispersive arcs induced by ionospheric and plasmaspheric occultation observed in GNSS signals recorded by the Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) payload during Blue Ghost Mission 1 (BGM1), in cislunar space and on the lunar surface.
